Every entry that accepts a host-supplied size (open, fromDecoder, updateResize, Reel::withSize) routes through here so the window is single-sourced: the frame block view() builds is cellsH lines x cellsW columns, and an unclamped pane is a multi-megabyte string per frame — a memory DoS at one constructor call, not a rendering curiosity.

Every text rung — including the direct Ansi256 row stream, whose rows carry their own SGR and split cleanly at \r\n — answers false: its frames are row-addressable.

Null when nothing was drawn or the current mode cannot delete by id.

Decoder implementation that wraps sugar-animation's pure-PHP GIF decoder.

MethodSummary
__construct(private readonly int $cellPxW = 10, private readonly int $cellPxH = 20)
open(string $source, int $cellsW, int $cellsH, float $fps, ?Mode $mode = null, float $startSec = 0.0, array $headers = []): void
static textSampled(): ?stringm14: non-null hint when the graphics path will silently degrade because this PHP has no image extension; null on a normal GD-capable host.

static setEmitCacheCeilingForTesting(?int $bytes): voidTest seam for the emit-cache byte ceiling; null restores MAX_EMIT_CACHE_BYTES. The ceiling is eviction policy, and policy is only honest if its trip point is unit-testable without shipping a 23 MiB fixture — the project's budget-seam idiom.
loopCount(): ?intThe playthrough count authored into the GIF's NETSCAPE2.0 loop extension, normalised by sugar-animation's AnimationDecoder::loopCount() — null means infinite (no extension present, or the raw-0 "loop forever" value; libnsgif's gif.c:862-871 reading), an integer N >= 2 means N total plays (raw values spell EXTRA repeats, so a total of 1 is not reachable from authored bytes — see playOnce()). null also answers before any open(); after close() it keeps reporting the last audited capture, because $bytes outlives close() by design.
playOnce(): boolTrue only when the bytes explicitly author exactly one playthrough. Unreachable from a valid NETSCAPE extension (raw 0 = forever, raw N > 0 = N+1 totals, so 1 is never produced — libnsgif documents "the only way to play the animation once is not to have this extension at all", gif.c:862-871, and the chicle CLI never consumes the loop field at all, it plays forever); this is the honest answer a host needs to know the difference between "the author said once" (some day, some other container) and "unauthored, play forever by policy".
static isGifFile(string $path): boolWhether $path names an existing file whose first six bytes are the GIF87a/GIF89a signature — container magic, not file extension.
getIterator(): \Generator
close(): void
reopen(string $source, int $cellsW, int $cellsH, float $fps, ?Mode $mode = null, float $startSec = 0.0, array $headers = []): void
reopensInPlace(): boolFalse — a seek cannot WALK this decoder's live cursor in place the way an injected double replays from its head; positions are taken by re-hydrating (the seconds route or the index walk both re-open from the captured bytes and land the cursor).
seeksBySeconds(): boolSV-M25/025: true — reopen() honours $startSec as a cursor jump over the open-time capture (the M38 single-capture law), so the Player's seconds routes land on it without any re-read.

VideoSource final class

Immutable value object describing a video source probed from ffprobe JSON output.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $path, public readonly int $width, public readonly int $height, public readonly float $duration, public readonly float $fps, public readonly bool $hasAudio)
static unprobed(string $path): selfThe metadata-free VO: everything a probe would answer stays unknown (zero dimensions, zero duration/fps, no audio). SV-M39/039 — a caller who pins fps themselves is declaring they know the stream, and fps is the ONLY probe product Player::open() still needs then, so the ffprobe child is skipped wholesale rather than consulted and ignored. Distinct from a FAILED probe's empty default because it is a choice, not a degradation: no child was ever spawned.

Cue final class

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly float $start, public readonly float $end, public readonly string $text)
contains(float $seconds): boolWhether $seconds falls within [start, end) — i.e. this cue is showing.

WebVtt final class

A parsed WebVTT subtitle track — a time-sorted list of Cues with a cueAt() lookup for the caption showing at a given playback time: two binary searches — rightmost start at or before the position, and the leftmost cue whose (prefix-maximum) end reaches it — so cues that provably cannot contain the position are never even looked at (SV-VTT/084). The walk that remains is bounded by real overlap, not by caption-free gaps, and the look runs on EVERY painted frame.

isEmpty(): bool

static sanitizeForTerminal(string $text): stringThe terminal-safety half of cleanText() on already tag-stripped text: newline/tab collapse, escape-sequence and zone-sentinel sweep, C0/DEL/C1 removal, and UTF-8 repair. Idempotent — running it over its own output changes nothing.
